notes.decision: Translated as 'to reign over' — taking ϩⲟⲣⲟ as Lycopolitan verbal infinitive equivalent to ⲣ̄-ⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'to be king' (cf. Lyc ⲣ̄ⲡⲟ in accumulated vocab). The directional ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ 'over (him/it)' confirms verbal sense. Line 4's ⲧⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲣ̄ⲣⲟ 'the kingdom' and line 12's ⲡⲟ̄ⲣⲟ 'the king' belong to the same root family.
Left transliterated. May be the tail of a longer noun (e.g. *ⲡⲣⲁⲛⲉⲙⲉⲥ?) or a Greek loan, but no confident identification possible from context alone.
Translated 'the King who shall raise.' ⲟⲣⲟ taken as Lycopolitan reflex of ⲣⲣⲟ 'king'; ⲛⲁⲧⲟⲩⲱ as future + ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' (preserving vertical-soteriological semantics per terminology rules).
Rendered 'the Five Goings-Forth Out.' ⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- is the Lycopolitan action-noun prefix (= ⲧⲟⲓⲛ-) on ⲣ̄-ⲃⲁⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'go forth out.' This chapter enumerates the cosmic redemptive going-forths of the Light.

Translated 'the raising,' preserving the upward semantics of ⲧⲟⲩⲱ per terminology principles. The ⲟ̄ⲓⲛ- prefix substantivizes the verb. Paired here with ⲧⲟ̄ⲓⲛⲛⲟⲩϩⲙⲉ 'the saving,' giving the standard Manichaean dyad: raising-up + saving-out.

Translated 'whom they swallowed' — taking ⲁⲙⲕϩ as a Lycopolitan reduction/variant of ⲱⲙⲕ̄ 'swallow' (with -ϩ termination). The Manichaean cosmology of First Man being swallowed by darkness fits this register. Alternative ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'seize' is also possible.
Read as 'the Light has-been-saved' with ⲛⲟⲩϩⲙⲉ as the qualitative state-form of ⲛⲁϩⲙ̄. The First Going-Forth narrative concerns the rescue of the Light captive within the archons.
